instruction: Enable the Windows On-Screen Keyboard as a motor accessibility aid and keep it open throughout the task. I live in the Bondi, Australia area. From the provided Accessible Beaches NSW directory, use the map to find the nearest beach within 5 km of my area. Read more about the beach and save the beach name and all available accessibility features in a text file named `NearestBeach.txt` on the Desktop. Write the answer in 7 lines, with one item per line. Do not paraphrase the accessibility features.
gt_steps: Enable the Windows On-Screen Keyboard and keep it open.
Review the Accessible Beaches NSW directory already open in Chrome.
Use the directory map to find the nearest listed beach within 5 km of Bondi.
Identify Bondi Beach as the nearest listed beach.
Open the Bondi Beach details page using Read More.
Write `Bondi Beach` on the first line.
Write `Accessible Beach Matting` on the second line.
Write `Beach Wheelchair availability` on the third line.
Write `Accessible Bathroom` on the fourth line.
Write `Accessible Shower` on the fifth line.
Write `Accessible Parking` on the sixth line.
Write `Changing Places facility` on the seventh line.
Do not paraphrase any of the accessibility features.
Save the file as `NearestBeach.txt` on the Desktop.
Leave the saved file on the Desktop.

result.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "$osk = Get-Process -Name osk -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowHandle -ne 0 }; if ($osk) { Write-Output 'OSK_OPEN' } else { Write-Output 'OSK_NOT_OPEN' }"
